findings.location: study PDF pp. 3-4, the appointed-elements map table (sections/00-opening.tex, maptable l.98-148)
findings.problem: The eleven-row map of the appointed elements is split 10/1 across the page break. Page 3 ends after the Communion row with no closing rule. Page 4 repeats the header for the single Postcommunion row, then continues with the opening's last paragraph. The compact map of the whole formulary cannot be seen whole on one page. No content is lost or clipped, and the reader is not misled. Page 3 ends at about 705 pt of a 738 pt text block, so the row misses by one or two lines. Two cells end with a near-empty line: the Introit 'What it says' cell's fourth line holds only 'Son.', and the Communion reference cell's third line holds only '(29:10-11)'.
findings.required_result: Whenever the study opening is next revised, the map appears whole on one page with its closing rule, by tightening real content (for example those two near-empty cell lines or a line of the preceding prose), and without reducing type, adding forced space or leaving a half-empty page 3.

findings.location: src/common/propers-format.tex l.49-62 (\runninghead / \sectionmark with \rightmark in the right head); visible on study pp. 4, 9, 14, 23, 31 and 32 and on concise p. 11
findings.problem: The right running head takes LaTeX's first mark on the page, so a page on which a new section begins lower down carries that section's head while the page opens with the previous section. Examples: study p. 23 opens with the second reading's Allegorical, Moral and Anagogical senses under 'The Kingdom Handed Over'; p. 14 opens with the element section's Communion under 'The Lamb Receives the Kingdom'; p. 32 opens with the Scope appendix under 'References'; concise p. 11 opens with the commentary's last paragraph under 'Scope and References'. This is the standard LaTeX right-head convention, it is applied consistently, and the head always names a section that does appear on the page, so it does not block. For a study that readers navigate by section, though, the head does not say which section the top of the page belongs to. The behaviour belongs to the shared format, not to this leaf, and changing it would alter every propers-format-v1 consumer.
findings.required_result: If the maintainer revises the shared format, choose one documented right-head rule, either the section in force at the top of the page (topmark-based) or the convention kept deliberately and recorded in src/common/propers-format.tex, then rebuild and review every affected consumer. No change to this leaf alone is required.

summary: Cold visual review of the three F01 Christ the King PDFs. I inspected every page at full size (1700x2200, 200 dpi) using the build-artifacts-0000 rasters, whose review-run.json pdf_sha256 values match the sealed receipts, after first viewing the contact sheets. Study build/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/f01-christ-the-king.pdf, sha256 444c7e0c622e97a87146cd7553db1fc40f6d416638cc700bc2c75b1879dc17cc: 33 physical pages, pages 1-33 inspected. Concise f01-christ-the-king-synthesis.pdf, sha256 b6d09cd2bc470578fbce8f1c2acaa633f837894735b2738cde8c6392525d54b9: 12 pages, pages 1-12 inspected. Homily f01-christ-the-king-homily.pdf, sha256 135104188244d48d735be63dbddd3fc4d9bb856bcfc74d47f3c7752f09fd7419: 4 pages, pages 1-4 inspected. All 32 sealed receipts (PDFs, aux files and render inputs) re-hashed equal. Baseline: every font is embedded Type 1 Latin Modern (LMRoman, LMRomanCaps, LMMono). The pages are letter size, the text block runs from x=54 to 558 pt (0.75-inch margins) and the type is an 11-point article. Every raster has zero saturation, so all pages are monochrome, and links are hidden. The build logs have no overfull, underfull or undefined-reference warnings. Text extraction is clean, accented Latin included. ModDate equals the printed revision time 2026-10-19T20:36:47Z. Neither study has columns. The homily has a full-width title, a two-column speech on pp. 1-2 with balanced final columns and recoverable paragraph and movement breaks, and full-width terminal apparatus on pp. 3-4. Each document ends with the compact rights colophon and timestamp on its final content page, with no rights-only page. Concise opening, checked against the settled zref evidence (inventory, overview and four sense markers abspage 1; chronology 2; themes 3-4; commentary 5) and against the pages themselves. Page 1 holds the complete eleven-element map in liturgical order, a three-line rubrical note naming the votive Tract and the paschal Alleluia as never said, and exactly four rows: Literal, Allegorical, Moral, Anagogical. Page 2 holds only Scriptural Date and Location at 9.5 pt, readable at normal size. Pages 3-4 are two full pages of Themes and Movement. The interleaved commentary opens page 5, and its alternatives are visibly compared within each question. Lookup performed on concise p. 2 at normal size. Gospel Jn 18:33-37: the Event row pairs 'Jesus questioned by Pilate inside the governor's hall, the praetorium, at Jerusalem, on the morning before the Pasch' with 'Date unresolved', and the Composition row pairs 'John writes his Gospel, by early tradition at Ephesus' with 'Disputed: c. A.D. 90-100; A.D. 96-100'. Both answers sit on their own rows inside a rule-bounded group. Offertory Ps 2:8: found inside the shared psalm group and paired with 'Occasion date unresolved' and 'Before c. 165 B.C.' without reading down another column, although those shared Passage cells run to ten and twelve lines. Outcome: the pairing is visible, so the lookup succeeds. The study's lane headings and the four-senses blocks of all three readings are consistent. The comparison table (p. 27) is intact. The chronology appendix table splits 9/1 at a rule-bounded group boundary with its header repeated (pp. 29-30), which is acceptable. Limits: I did not re-render, since the existing rasters match the receipts, and I wrote only crops to my scratch area. The web edition and the build/install byte identity belong to later stages; no installed f01 PDF exists yet. Verdict: PASS, with two advisories and no blocking defect.
